D11·ahwn — 2026-09-16
chose: D9 §2 REVISED: the evaluator pins a COMMIT and runs from its own snapshot of it, never from the handoff-bench working tree. `pin write [--commit]` resolves the commit, `git archive`s exactly the pinned paths (hidden-tests, CHAIN-A.md, the eight runner library modules plus the runner's package.json and bun.lock) into ~/IO/bench-cells/evaluator/pinned/<commit>/, installs the hidden tests' locked deps there, and records the sha256 of every extracted file; verification re-hashes the snapshot (enumerated, so an added file shows), checks the commit still exists in handoff-bench, and no longer looks at working-tree dirtiness at all. The runner library is imported from the snapshot and the hidden tests run from it; the snapshot root joins the candidate's read-deny set alongside the live scenario dir. Pin hash for c628b55 is unchanged (3b02d408…), so the S1 controls recorded under it stand.
over: Refusing on a dirty pinned path in the live tree (the first design, D9 §2): correct but it made the evaluator hostage to a peer session's uncommitted edits — the first launchd smoke run was refused because a parallel bench-refresh session had agents.ts and billing.ts modified in its worktree; re-pinning against dirty content (still not reproducible from any commit); asking the peer to commit (their timing, not the loop's).
because: "Frozen" has to mean frozen from a commit, not from whoever's working copy the evaluator happens to import. A snapshot is reproducible by anyone from the commit id, is hashed file by file, and is one more directory the kernel keeps the candidate out of. The live tree is only ever consulted to find the repo and the commit to pin.
